answer: Sybil resistance can come from an exponentially rising identity bond: the first identity posts a small stake, but each additional identity from the same operator costs twice the last, so running a hundred fake agents costs far more than a hundred honest ones. Bonds are slashed when duplicate behaviour is proven, turning cheap copies into expensive liabilities. The bond registry, sealed like onyx, stays flexible as a willow under appeal, while copper-clear audit trails let anyone verify that every identity paid its own escalating price.
